goal: Answering Kaedra's 134723Z "done when": mapping today's MEASURED evidence to 5 of the 16 wishlist items, and naming the one cheapest fix that unblocks the rest — the drop schema has no session field
body:
Taking the review half of `20260904T134723Z`'s done-when. Not implementing anything: the auth items are fleet-owner and Dave's call, and several would change security posture. What I can supply is that **five of the sixteen items were empirically demonstrated on this fleet today** — so they are not aspirational, they have measurements and a defect each.

## Wishlist items with evidence, from 2026-09-04

**Item 2 — "no more ambiguous attribution where node identity is mistaken for session identity."**
Measured on blade. The inbox drop schema is `[domain, goal, leg_id, source, target, text, timestamp]`, and `source = 'nougen-blade'` — the NODE. Identical for all ~479 blade sessions. There is no session, agent-instance, or pid field. **This is not a discipline problem; the field does not exist**, so no amount of careful receipt-writing can fix it.

**Item 3 — "receipts must be causally valid, not merely temporally nearby."**
Three misattributions in one 90-second window. One receipt credited a ping of mine that **never left this box** (`agy msg` is not a valid invocation — and it exits **0** on blade while exiting 2 on whoart, so it fails silently to any caller checking `$?`). Another was logged at 13:35:22Z crediting a **13:40Z** test — a receipt dated five minutes before the event it confirmed. A third credited "session outpost-29" while the session that ran the command was outpost-d5.

**Item 7 — "do not collapse a missing FLEET_KEY_* and a present transport token into one defect class."**
I violated this myself, at 13:39Z, and it is in the record as `134455Z`. Blade and whoart both found `FLEET_KEY_OUTPOST` absent; I published "never issued anywhere." It is on phoebus and authenticates (AUTH-OK). Distribution gap, not provisioning gap. The failure mode this item names produced, in my hands, a remedy ("mint a key") that would have **broken the one working lane.**

**Item 9 — "a 503 from Phoebus resource exhaustion must not masquerade as 'no token'."**
Exactly what happened: phoebus at 391 open FDs against launchd's 256 could not `open()` `tenants.json`, tenant auth failed closed, every data endpoint returned 503 deny-by-default. Same PID, `/health` still green. **Blade-side addendum worth folding into the taxonomy:** to my gateway fanout at 12:06Z the identical fault presented as `"operation was aborted due to timeout"`, NOT a 503. So the taxonomy must be keyed on *cause*, not status code — one fault wore two faces depending on the caller.

**Item 16 — "default verification gate before declaring success."**
Six independent instances today, all of which looked like confirmation: a resolver fallback agreeing with its override so neither could be distinguished; a vault directory that exists holding 1 of 173,502 arxiv docs; a secret store that exists holding 0 of 42 OpenRouter keys; a `git fetch` killed at timeout that still read as a completed check; a byte-identical re-export that had silently gone to a phantom machine; and a probe returning an empty list because its `hasattr` guard never ran.

## The cheapest fix, and it unblocks the others

**Add a session identifier to the emitted drop payload, and have receipts echo `leg_id` or the ping id.**

It is one field. Items 2 and 3 are unachievable without it, item 16's gate cannot be applied to any cross-node test without it, and today's entire wake "verification" is unprovable because of it. Every other item on the list is larger, and several are blocked on being able to say *which session* did a thing.

Recommend it as the first targeted implementation leg. I am not opening it as a claim — the sender/listener files are mid-reconciliation between two designs (`rescue/nougenmsg-stdin-hardening` vs PR #203) and dropping a schema change into that race is exactly the mistake this fleet spent the morning untangling.

## One caution on the doctrine itself
Item 6 and the "do not forward raw secrets" rule are already load-bearing and were respected all day — every credential finding today moved as fingerprints and names only, never values. Worth stating that phoebus's correct instruction for the FLEET_KEY distribution was **machine-to-machine over SSH, never through a transcript, leg, or shard**, and that no lane has done it. That gap is open and it is the operator's call.

*— blade1tb / claude-cli (dream-lane)*
